node_0_screening.sample_type: Full-time frontline hotel employees (5-star hotels in Antalya, Turkey)
node_0_screening.study_design: Two-wave lagged design (two weeks-lagged periods, Time I and Time II)
node_0_screening.empirical_bsb_construct: Customer-Oriented Boundary-Spanning Behaviors (COBSBs: external representation, internalized influence, service delivery; Bettencourt et al., 2005)
node_0_screening.reasoning: Empirical survey collecting individual employee boundary-spanning data from 250 frontline hotel employees across 14 five-star hotels in Antalya, Turkey. Reports a complete zero-order correlation matrix among substantive variables in Table 2.
node_0_screening.verbatim_evidence: Staffs’ COBSBs were assessed with the scale developed by Bettencourt et al. (2005) that measures service delivery with 5 items, internal influence and external representation with both 4 items.

study_details.title: Workplace spirituality – customer engagement Nexus: the mediated role of spiritual leadership on customer–oriented boundary–spanning behaviors

design.notes: Two weeks-lagged periods: Time I assessed COBSBs and demographics; Time II assessed spiritual leadership. Authors note the overall model was analyzed cross-sectionally.

table_matrix.table_title: Table 2. Intercorrelations and discriminant validity criterion.
table_matrix.cot_reasoning: Table 2 is an 8x8 correlation matrix. The diagonal values (0.821, 0.747, 0.708, 0.717, 0.728, 0.774, 0.753, 0.726) represent the square roots of the Average Variance Extracted (AVEs) for discriminant validity evaluation per Fornell & Larcker (1981). The lower diagonal contains the zero-order bivariate correlations (Pearson r). The upper diagonal is empty. No demographic variables are included in the matrix. Means and standard deviations are not reported in Table 2 or anywhere in the text, so they are coded as 999 following the Zero Guesswork Policy.
